reason: The recycling cells are shown breaking down worn red cells, which should start the iron-recovery goal.
expectation: The recycling cells will break down the worn cells and make their iron available for reuse.

effect: The worn cells yielded iron carried in blood, so it can now be taken to the marrow for reuse.
reaction: It makes sense that the recycling cells remain intact while the iron is recovered.
reason: The marrow makes blood cells, and the goal says to use the recovered iron in new red cells.

choice.combine: Iron recovered from old blood cells

expectation: The marrow will use the recovered iron to make new red blood cells.

effect: The recovered iron became part of haemoglobin in new red cells, completing the blood-cell goal. The skin-cell goal remains.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the iron reused while the marrow stays intact.
reason: The picture shows these materials moving toward the dividing skin cells to support their growth.

choice.combine: Dividing cells at the skin's base
choice.with: Water, glucose and cell building materials

expectation: The cells will use the supplied materials to grow replacement skin cells.

effect: The materials supported new skin cells while the base cells and continuous covering remained. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The picture of new cells growing underneath while old flakes leave made the replacement process clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using recovered iron in marrow was most worthwhile because it showed how material from old cells becomes part of the oxygen-carrying protein in new cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: The skin-cell combination was straightforward from the picture, so it involved less figuring out, although the result was clear.

surprise.text: I noticed that the base population stays in place while its descendants move outward and become flatter.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary: the pictures and goals explained why the materials belonged with the cells or marrow.

continue.text: I might continue to see another body process connected to what was already built, though these three predictable combinations alone were not a strong hook.
